question: Prescribing a strong opioid as the sole analgesic is the safest and most effective approach to postoperative pain management after day-case surgery.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. The standard approach to postoperative pain management is multimodal: paracetamol + NSAID + opioid (as needed), with opioid-sparing as the goal. Opioid monotherapy increases side-effects (nausea, sedation, respiratory depression) without superior analgesia, and is especially problematic in day-case patients who need to be safe for discharge.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is FALSE. Multimodal analgesia (combining paracetamol, NSAIDs, and opioids at lower doses) achieves better pain control with fewer opioid side-effects (nausea, sedation, respiratory depression) than opioid monotherapy — which is particularly important in day-case patients who must be safe for discharge.
